newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - March 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - March 31.

text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in the Japanese press on Monday, as reported by Kyodo news agency.
-- Japan's economic recovery is slowing down.
-- Government and private sector plan to acquire 380 billion yen worth of land under land liquidity plan.
-- Nippon Credit Bank Ltd president Hiroshi Kubota is expected to resign.
-- Former Chief Cabinet Secretary Yohei Kono defends 1993 government decision on stance over "comfort women" issue.
-- Archbishop Cipriani suggests Peru hostages would be released in three stages.

-- More than 40 percent of former bureacrats from Health and Welfare Ministry's social welfare and old-age welfare bureaus get "amakudari" jobs -- plum positions in the private sector after they leave office.
